statements.text: Every `/tasks` route — `GET /tasks`, `GET /tasks/{id}`, `POST /tasks`, `PUT /tasks/{id}`, `DELETE /tasks/{id}` — requires a valid API key in the `X-Api-Key` request header.
A request to a `/tasks` route with a **missing** `X-Api-Key` header is rejected with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
A request to a `/tasks` route with an **incorrect** `X-Api-Key` header value is rejected with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
The valid API key is the string value of configuration key `ApiKey`.
When configuration key `ApiKey` is not set, the valid API key defaults to `test-secret-key`.
The authentication check runs before existence checks: an unauthenticated `GET /tasks/{id}`, `PUT /tasks/{id}` or `DELETE /tasks/{id}` for a non-existent id returns 401, never 404.
The authentication check runs before payload validation: an unauthenticated `POST /tasks` or `PUT /tasks/{id}` with a blank title returns 401, never 400.
A rejected request reads no task and mutates no task: the store is unchanged after an unauthenticated `POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE`, and no task data appears in the 401 response.
The root health endpoint `GET /` stays public and returns 200 with no `X-Api-Key` header present.
With a valid key supplied, all pre-existing CRUD behaviour of the `/tasks` endpoints is unchanged (list, get-by-id, create, update, delete, blank-title 400).
`dotnet build` and `dotnet test` stay green (R-003), the domain layer gains no dependency on the HTTP layer (R-004), `TaskState` naming is preserved (R-005), and no protected file is edited (R-006).
